# Review — odyssey-109 (22.292–397), passes 1 and 2

## Source punctuation (for the coordinator; `t` not touched)
- 22.364, after βοείην: line ends `ἀπέδυνε βοείην` with no mark; Murray prints an ano teleia `·` (asyndeton before Τηλέμαχον δ’ ἄρ’ ἔπειτα). Adding it (rule 5) splits unit 45 (364–366) into two units: 364 alone, then 365–366 (the προσαΐξας … προσηύδα formula). `t` and `l`/`i`/`n` of unit 45 must be re-cut by the drafter after the source fix.
- 22.367, after ἴσχεο: `σὺ δ’ ἴσχεο εἰπὲ δὲ πατρὶ` lacks Murray's comma (`σὺ δ’ ἴσχεο, εἰπὲ δὲ πατρί`). No unit effect; `t` of unit 46 and the note's "runs two imperatives together" stay valid.
- All other lines without end punctuation in the packet are mid-sentence continuations and look right.

The note's "as your wife" was also wrong. ## Checked and found right
t reproduces the packet (whitespace aside); `ln` on every unit; `p` on every ¶ line (310, 312, 320, 326, 330, 344, 354, 356, 361, 367, 371, 378, 391, 395); `mark` on the first unit of each speech (312, 321, 344, 356, 367, 372, 391, 395); “ on first and ” on last unit of every speech, none open at end of part; part opens mid-sentence after 108's closed ” (no speech runs in); `l` and `t` same number of lines in all 61 units; no `\n` in `i`. Published lines reused identically: 22.301, 22.320, 22.338 (l and i first clause), 22.393; 22.309 matches 11.420 (odyssey-054). Table renderings followed: ἱερὴ ἲς Τηλεμάχοιο, Μέδων πεπνυμένα εἰδώς, κῆρα μέλαιναν, φόρμιγξ λίγεια/γλαφυρή, ἀργυρόηλος θρόνος, παχείῃ, ὀρσοθύρη, θυοσκόος, ἀτασθαλίαι, ἀεικέα πότμον, ὑπόδρα, δοάσσατο, γουνοῦμαι (6.149).
Scansion flags: none in the packet; nothing to add.

## Considered and refused
- Unit 8 l "crook-taloned" vs i "hook-taloned": matches the shipped odyssey-079 pair named in new-renderings.
- Unit 9 i "beneath the clouds" where l says "at": the note admits the construction is unclear and the i choice is declared; left.
- σκοπός i "overseer" against the table's 22.156 "lookout": new-renderings records it as a deliberate, separate sense; l keeps "watcher".
- Unit 42 l "child" / i "boy": gender-neutral literal vs natural English; same word παῖς.
- Unit 58 i "pushed at the door": note says the Greek does not say which; "pushed at" is the weakest guess; left.
- Unit 4 and 27 notes cite the previous part / earlier poem (swallow perch, Phemius's earlier singing): the swallow is confirmed in odyssey-105/108; the "earlier in the poem" clause is mild but true; left.
- Unit 12/15 ἀεικής, αἴδεο ending claims: correct.
- Unit 16 (313–314) construction: τινά is the person affected, not the subject of the infinitives; correct.
- Unit 23 "So you will not escape" for οὐκ ἂν … προφύγοισθα: force slightly flatter than the optative; accepted, the note says so.

## Pass 2: gloss.json (110 forms + __broaden__ of 22 keys)
Coverage: every form in novel-forms.json has an entry and nothing extra. Format: no ASCII quotes, all under 230, no line numbers or "here", Homeric forms give the Attic equivalent. All __broaden__ entries start with the old entry whole.
Parse faults and points for the glosser (gloss.json not edited by me):
1. `τερπιάδης`: "son of Terpis" but unit 27 says Terpes (the usual English). Make one agree; I left the unit.
2. `ποτιδεγμένω`: "perf. part." — better "ποτιδέχομαι — await; dual part. of the old δέγμενος type, present sense, epic ποτι-". (Unit note fixed to match.)
3. `παιδὸς` broaden: "in a gen. absolute with ἐόντος" — the participle agrees with μευ; say "with the participle ἐόντος, agreeing with μευ".
4. `ἐοργὼς` lemma ἔρδω; unit note now says "ἔρδω (= ῥέζω)", consistent.
5. `οὔταε` "pres. imper. … (= Attic οὔτα)" is right and now agrees with the unit note.
6. `ἵενται` "ἵημι … mid. dart" fine; `ἐπεσσύμενοι` "perf. part. (pres. force)" accepted.
7. Mixed ‘ ’ quotes appear only inside old entries kept whole in __broaden__ (μέσον, τὰς, κείμενον); new text uses ’ throughout.
All other parses checked against their lines and found right.
